quotes.quote: We applied two types of regression models (details in 2.3.1 and 2.3.4), using Bayesian inference applied using the R‐INLA package (Lindgren and Rue 2015 ).

To establish interpolated temporal trends covering the entire study period, for all four segments as well as the total study area, we modelled annual abundances using generalised additive mixed models (GAMMs).

G1.rationale: The principal results are produced by Bayesian GAMMs/GLMMs on collated aerial survey data, which a third party can re-run if the data are available.

quotes.quote: At its peak in 2016, the modelled abundance of calves across the entire study area was 222 (CI 186–258) individuals. This has slightly declined to 200 (CI 137–264) individuals in 2024 (Figure 2 ).

At the modelled peak in 2011, the number of unaccompanied individuals across the entire area was 248 individuals (CI 197–299), which dropped to an estimated 84 (CI −1 to 170) individuals only in 2024 (Figure 2 ). This is a decline of 66.1% in 13 years.

G2.rationale: The paper reports several principal quantitative results; the modelled calf abundance in 2024 (200, CI 137–264) is a primary numerical endpoint from the GAMM, and the 66.1% decline in unaccompanied individuals is a principal effect. The hierarchy selects the primary numerical endpoint first.

Predicted values were generated by simulating 1000 values per segment, ranging from 1976 to 2024, and taking the mean of these values per segment per year. Predicted values were converted back to absolute abundances (counts, using segment lengths).

specification.input_notes: The Dryad deposit (9s4mw6mth) is listed but contains no files in the provided listing. The analysis inputs are the collated aerial survey abundance records from 1976–2024, which are not available as listed files.
specification.comparison_metric: The observed value is the modelled calf abundance in 2024 extracted from the GAMM output; it is compared to the reported value of 200 individuals.
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Scalars within displayed rounding bin: the modelled estimate should round to 200 individuals, and the credible interval should round to 137–264.
specification.specification_gaps: The exact priors and smoothing parameters for the GAMM are not fully specified; the method for simulating 1000 values per segment is not detailed; the treatment of missing data and the exact model selection procedure are not fully described.
